title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Clusters generated from only trigonal-bipyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, only square-pyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)}, or only octahedral {Ln6(μ6-O)(μ3-OH)8} units are rare compared with triangle- and cubane-based families.
explanation: The review says only one cluster built from the trigonal-bipyramidal block has been reported, Dy10, formed by two {Ln5(μ3-OH)6} units bridged by isonicotinate. Square pyramids account for Ln9 and templated Ln104; octahedra account for Ln16 and Zn4@Ln24, the last of which also contains transition-metal ions. Anion templation is again noted as important for Ln104.
scope: Lanthanide clusters whose cores are assigned to a single one of these three motifs.
caveats: Rarity is relative to the literature covered through 2017 and to the authors’ structural classification; Ln104 shows that the square-pyramidal motif can still reach very high nuclearity when templated.
